faq.a: The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index for a portfolio: add up the square of each holding's weight in percent, so a holding at 50% contributes 2,500. The score runs from near 0 to 10,000. Under 1,500 reads as diversified, 1,500 to 2,500 as moderate, and over 2,500 as concentrated.
faq.q: What is the HHI concentration score?

faq.a: How much the whole portfolio would fall if only the largest holding dropped, by 20% and by 50%. It is the largest weight times the fall, so a 50% holding falling 50% cuts the portfolio by 25%.
faq.q: What does the largest holding fall show?

faq.a: Up to 6. Enter at least 2 holdings with values above zero. Leave the rest blank.
